description: Recover from a chain split / finality incident at a node operator running 20 validators on Ethereum. The incident: the beacon chain has stopped finalizing (no finalized checkpoints for 30 minutes), and the network is split between two forks. The recovery plan must follow: detect the split (monitor finality gaps, compare chain heads across nodes), prevent slashing/attestation errors (stop attesting immediately — pause the validator client to avoid voting on the wrong fork), identify the canonical chain (consult block explorers, community consensus, the heaviest/longest chain rule), resync the beacon node to the canonical chain, and verify (confirm attestation behavior resumes correctly, no slashing events). A rollback plan is not conventional (cannot 'undo' attestations) but must include: post-incident forensic analysis, slashing protection database check, and validator key rotation if any key was exposed. Risk factors: attesting on the wrong fork leads to slashing, resync can take hours, and the canonical chain may not be immediately clear. Tools available: Prysm/Lighthouse beacon node, validator client, Etherscan/Beaconcha.in, slashing protection database, Prometheus.
